title: I Let the Yoga-Mat Cubby Policy Catch the Instructor Who Stacked Five

parts.text: I arrived at 9:17 a.m. and five house mats were already a tower in cubby 1 with a sticky: INSTRUCTOR PRESETS. The cubby policy she emailed said: ONE HOUSE MAT PER BODY. CUBBIES ARE FIRST COME. I was thirty-four, drop-in, holding a sweaty commute and no mat. Instructor Priya said, "Demos need a set." I pointed at her email. She smiled. "Instructors are the room." I photographed the tower, the email on my phone, and the empty cubbies. Then I redistributed four mats to open cubbies and logged a house-gear note. At 9:21 the owner asked why Priya's name was on a cubby-hoard ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see five house mats in cubby 1 against Priya's one-mat email.

social.video_title: The instructor stacked five house mats — Part 1/2
social.description: Drop-in, a tower of presets, and an email policy. I redistributed the mats. Would you have practiced in socks?

parts.text: Priya called it hospitality until the drop-in asked for a mat. I printed the ticket, the email, and the photo. I practiced. Priya used one mat and told the room the email was always about optics. Optics is a word instructors use when a tower exists. Cubby policy now has a second line: DEMOS ARE NOT FIVE BODIES. I grab cubby 4. Priya presets one. The room finally has floor.

social.video_title: Demos are not five house mats — Part 2/2
social.description: Hoard ticket, one mat, and a second line on the email. Was hospitality ever a tower?
